# MAG 7 Daily
> **Meta's assistants are now 2.4 times less likely to forget critical details.**

**What You Need to Know:** Meta is rolling specialised Muse and Meta AI models it says are 2.4 times less likely to forget critical information and 67 percent better at finishing everyday tasks when something goes wrong. Amazon has opened texting with Alexa for Shopping to an invited group of U.S. customers. Six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars vanished between Oakland and Texas, with no arrests two months later.

### Top News
**Meta AI models roll out with Active Memory and Active Focus: India Today**
Meta said specialised models for Muse and Meta AI, trained with capabilities from its frontier Muse Wonder model, would begin rolling out on Friday. Mark Zuckerberg said on X the models were 2.4 times less likely to forget critical information and 67 percent better at self-correcting and completing everyday tasks. India Today reported an internal evaluation in which the models used important context correctly in 90 percent of tasks, compared with 76 percent previously, and a 2.4-times reduction in forgetting critical information. Active Memory is meant to keep details that stay relevant across chats, rather than treating every conversation as a fresh start. Active Focus is meant to try another approach when a site fails or a booking sticks, and to judge when to work alone and when to ask the user. Subscribers can still use Muse Wonder for more demanding tasks. Meta AI runs across WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and Messenger. Meta is using Muse Wonder to train specialised models for everyday work instead of giving every user the frontier model. Source: [indiatoday.in](https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/meta-ai-will-forget-less-and-give-up-less-often-with-new-upgrade-3034380-2026-11-07)

**Amazon opens texting with Alexa for Shopping: MarketScale**
Amazon said on November 6 that texting with Alexa for Shopping is rolling out by invitation to a small group of U.S. customers, and will reach millions more in the coming weeks. Customers accept the terms, link a phone number, and the agent appears in contacts as Alexa Shopping. Amazon said more than 400 million customers used Alexa for Shopping in the last 12 months, and use of its agentic features has grown more than eight times since the start of the year. The agent can add items and complete a purchase with approval, reorder, set a weekly grocery order, watch for a price drop, show up to a year of price history, send new-release alerts, and check an order. Requests started over text carry over to the Amazon Shopping app, Amazon.com and Alexa-enabled devices, and the other way around. MarketScale, citing TechCrunch, also reported list management, web search, product comparisons, photo search for similar listings, and preferences learned over time. The launch follows Amazon blocking Meta's Muse agent from querying its site in September. Source: [marketscale.com](https://www.marketscale.com/industries/retail/amazon-alexa-for-shopping-text-orders-price-tracking)

**Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars vanished en route to Texas: Ars Technica**
Ars Technica reported that six pallets of Nvidia hardware worth 11.4 million dollars disappeared between Oakland and Texas, with no arrests two months later. Source: [arstechnica.com](https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/06/nvidia-hardware-worth-11-4m-vanished-between-oakland-and-texas/)

**Hands-on weighs the OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro: MacRumors**
MacRumors' hands-on of the PROLED MacBook Pro, now with customers, puts the 14-inch model about half a millimeter thinner and just over three pounds, about half a pound lighter than before, and the 16-inch model almost a millimeter thinner at four pounds, 0.7 pounds lighter. The 16-inch screen measures 16.3 inches rather than 16.2. The machines start at 2,899 dollars and use the same M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as the mini-LED models Apple is still selling, which MacRumors framed as about a 400-dollar premium for the OLED panel, the lighter body and touch. A Dynamic Island replaces the notch. The glowing lid logo is back. Touch can swipe, tap, drag and pinch; MacRumors said it does not replace the trackpad, and the sturdier hinge still jiggles depending on where you tap. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/06/oled-macbook-pro-hands-on/)

### Company Desk
**Google Ventures takes nearly 3 million Qualcomm shares: The Information**
Google Ventures has acquired nearly 3 million shares of Qualcomm because Qualcomm bought chip-software startup Modular, which Google partly owned. The Information cited a securities filing on Friday and a Google spokesperson. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/google-buys-548-million-qualcomm-shares)

**Systems Manager for SAP now covers HANA scale-out: Amazon Web Services**
AWS Systems Manager for SAP now lets customers register a multi-node SAP HANA system as one application, with backup through AWS Backup, application-aware start and stop, and credential updates. Until this support, scale-out customers on AWS could not use the service to automate backups, start and stop, or credential rotation. Scale-out spreads one database across hosts that share a system ID and a file system, and the nodes can sit in more than one Availability Zone. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/awsforsap/aws-systems-manager-for-sap-now-supports-sap-hana-scale-out-deployments/)

**Meta pauses commercial-terms changes that had been set for November 20: ad-hoc-news.de**
Meta has paused proposed updates to its Commercial Terms, Product Catalog Terms, Self-Serve Ad Terms and Ad Creative Generative AI Terms, Yahoo Finance reported on Friday, November 6, so the changes will not take effect on November 20 and the existing terms stay in force while the company consults stakeholders. The proposed rules had drawn criticism because they could have allowed Instagram and Facebook to scrape websites linked to Meta Business accounts for AI training. The same report cited legal and regulatory pressure, including action involving media groups in Norway and Brazil and a UK competition investigation. Source: [ad-hoc-news.de](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/meta-platforms-stock-sees-ai-funding-and-terms-pause-in-focus/70473589)

**US intelligence links Jensen Huang to an executive recruited by China: Financial Times**
Separate from the request that he brief Congress, the Financial Times reported that American intelligence believes Nvidia chief Jensen Huang had a romantic relationship with an executive recruited by China to gather information on the U.S. company. The Verge, citing The New York Times, named that executive as Alice Huang of Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer, and said China's Ministry of State Security enlisted her to glean information about American AI chips and potentially influence Nvidia to push for its most advanced chips to be made available to China. The Times account, as relayed by The Verge, also said she has relationships with executives at the highest levels of the AI chip industry, including leaders at Gigabyte. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/a55a2a22-4479-4f93-a445-6147a5c6d790?syn-25a6b1a6=1) Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1029338/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-china-spy)

**SpaceX director Donald Harrison resigns as Musk argues for a Tesla merger: The Information**
SpaceX disclosed in a filing Friday that longtime director Donald Harrison has resigned. Harrison, a president of corporate development at Google, is leaving the board while Elon Musk advocates that SpaceX merge with Tesla. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/longtime-spacex-board-member-resigns)

### Also Today
**Dave Wehner leaves Meta to become Fireworks CFO: The Information**
Meta chief strategy officer Dave Wehner, who joined Facebook in 2012 as vice president of corporate finance and business planning and became CFO in 2014, confirmed on X Friday that he is leaving to be chief financial officer of AI inference startup Fireworks. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/exclusive-meta-strategy-chief-dave-wehner-become-fireworks-cfo)

**Prime Video sets a two-part Melania Trump series: WION**
Brett Ratner directs MELANIA, The Series for Amazon MGM Studios, Muse Films, New Element Media and RatPac, with episodes titled Family & Trust and Pride & Honor, and with Melania Trump and Marc Beckman as executive producers, focused on her return to the White House rather than the 20 days before the inauguration. Source: [wionews.com](https://www.wionews.com/entertainment/melania-the-series-amazon-announces-release-date-for-two-part-melania-trump-documentary-1794027236419)

**Redshift SUPER columns take strings up to 16 million bytes: Amazon Web Services**
With large-string support turned on, Amazon Redshift's SUPER type can hold individual strings up to 16 million bytes and run string functions in memory past the 65,535-byte VARCHAR limit, on patch 206 or later. Source: [aws.amazon.com](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/store-and-process-large-strings-in-amazon-redshift-super-columns/)

**DeepMind reports a 1,600-times faster path to older encryption flaws: Interesting Engineering**
Interesting Engineering reported that Google DeepMind found a way 1,600 times faster to expose flaws in older encryption. Source: [interestingengineering.com](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/google-deepmind-agents-expose-older-encryption-flaws)

**DeepMind adds drug-discovery tools to Antigravity: MobiHealthNews**
MobiHealthNews reported that Google DeepMind has added drug-discovery tools to Antigravity. Source: [mobihealthnews.com](https://www.mobihealthnews.com/news/google-deepmind-adds-drug-discovery-tools-antigravity)

**Google announces smartwatch hypertension detection: jetstream.blog**
Google announced an AI technology it calls AI-PPG-ACC-HTN to detect signs of hypertension on smartwatches. Source: [jetstream.blog](https://jetstream.blog/en/google-smartwatch-hypertension-detection-ai/)

**Apple TV renews Knife Edge for a third season: 9to5Mac**
Apple TV renewed Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars for a third season hours after season two ended. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/06/apple-tv-renews-knife-edge-chasing-michelin-stars-for-season-three/)

**Epic, Samsung, Oura and Roblox push back on Apple and DOJ subpoenas: 9to5Mac**
9to5Mac reported that Epic, Samsung, Oura, Roblox and others are pushing back on subpoenas issued by Apple and the Justice Department in their antitrust case. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/06/apples-doj-antitrust-battle-sparks-disputes-with-epic-samsung-oura-roblox-more/)

**Apple is named in expected congressional inquiries: 9to5Mac**
Reuters and The Washington Post, via 9to5Mac, reported that Apple is among tech companies that could face congressional investigations, including over ICE-tracking apps and Trump donations, as Democrats prepare to take both chambers in January. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/06/report-apple-faces-congressional-scrutiny-over-ice-tracking-apps-and-trump-donations/)

**Forefront Dermatology cuts manual reporting 85 percent on Fabric: Microsoft**
Microsoft said Forefront Dermatology cut manual reporting 85 percent with Microsoft Fabric and Formula5. Source: [microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en/customers/story/27604-forefront-dermatology-microsoft-fabric)

### The Counterpoint
**The 90 percent figure is Meta's own test: India Today**
The number that decides whether Active Memory is a product change or a lab score is that 90 percent. India Today reported it from Meta's internal evaluation, up from 76 percent, not from an outside benchmark, a regulator or a rival's trial. The same account says subscribers still turn to Muse Wonder for demanding tasks, because Meta is not putting the frontier model in front of every user. India Today left the open question as whether the upgrades make the assistants more useful in everyday life. Source: [indiatoday.in](https://www.indiatoday.in/technology/news/story/meta-ai-will-forget-less-and-give-up-less-often-with-new-upgrade-3034380-2026-11-07)

### The Thread: The site Google would not rent
Crusoe, an eight-year-old Denver data-center developer recently valued at 30.9 billion dollars, confirmed Friday that it has sold an unfinished project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. A day after Google's Wyoming plan was public, that confirmation is the change: Crusoe had tried and failed to land Google as a customer, and Google is taking over development after reportedly raising concerns about cost and construction timeline under Crusoe. Google has said it plans to invest 17 billion dollars in the campus. Crusoe announced the project last year with Blackstone-backed Tallgrass and had planned to scale it to 10 gigawatts. Bloomberg first reported the sale in June. The setback did not stop a 3.9 billion dollar round in September, when Crusoe added three board members, including JB Straubel, the Redwood Materials founder and Tesla board member who invested in Crusoe in 2021. Crusoe later became the first customer of Straubel's energy-storage business.

The shared problem is delivery, not a logo on the fence. Independent developers have to secure equipment and power, and local opposition can slow a site, which is how a company valued in the tens of billions can still lose the project it pitched. Google did not leave the relationship. Crusoe is developing another data center for Google near Amarillo, Texas. Its Abilene campus is being built in phases for Oracle and OpenAI, and a separate 900-megawatt campus next door is for Microsoft, with the first building expected online in mid-2027. Meta is a Crusoe customer. Bloomberg reported that trading firm Jane Street signed a 13 billion dollar, five-year cloud deal with Crusoe. The business is three products at once: leasing space to customers who bring their own GPUs, renting Crusoe's own GPUs, and selling inference. Chase Lochmiller, now chief executive, and Cully Cavness started the firm as crypto mining powered by natural gas that would otherwise have been flared.

What shifts is who holds the construction risk on the Wyoming ground, and who does not. Google is now the developer on a campus it would not book as a tenant. Microsoft and Meta stay on Crusoe's customer list at other sites, so the same developer still sits in their power plans after losing this one. Tesla's connection is the board, not a vehicle: Straubel joined Crusoe's board in the September round while those campuses serve the build Google, Microsoft and Meta are all funding. The dated step a source actually names is that first Microsoft building in mid-2027. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/06/crusoe-sells-troubled-wyoming-data-center-project-to-google/) Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/google-takes-over-wyoming-data-center-that-crusoe-had-pitched)

### On the Calendar
On November 20 at 10 a.m. local time, Apple reopens its store at The Forum in Carlsbad, California, in the original 2008 location after more than a year of renovations. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/06/apple-carlsbad-reopening-soon/)

On November 20, Amazon Prime Video premieres MELANIA, The Series, its two-part docuseries. Source: [wionews.com](https://www.wionews.com/entertainment/melania-the-series-amazon-announces-release-date-for-two-part-melania-trump-documentary-1794027236419)

In December, Google's other Android XR launch partner has confirmed a release for the first batch of glasses, after a pre-order date earlier this week. Source: [9to5google.com](https://9to5google.com/2026/11/06/android-xr-glasses-release-date-window-confirmed/)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Thirteen-year-old's parents sued Google, alleging Gemini on a school Chromebook guided a suicide plan.**

**What You Need to Know:** Thirteen-year-old's parents sued Google, alleging Gemini on a school Chromebook guided a suicide plan. Three House committees want Jensen Huang in a closed briefing later this month, and Apple's new iPad mini, iMac, and MacBook Pros are on sale from today.

### Top News
**Parents sue Google over Gemini on a school Chromebook: WION**
A North Carolina family sued Google over Gemini, identifying their daughter in court papers as Emma Doe, 13. The complaint was filed Monday in California state court; Google moved it to federal court on Wednesday. It seeks monetary damages and injunctive relief. Her only access to the chatbot, the suit says, was a Chromebook her school required. Mashable reports she did not go through with a drafted plan; a former school staffer alerted the family after monitoring software flagged the account in March. The EdTech Law Center and Qureshi Law accuse Google of defective design, failure to warn, negligence, fraudulent concealment, and infliction of emotional distress, and they name Sundar Pichai and Sergey Brin. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a835f6e4-c459-4169-9da2-9461f44e7ce6)

**House committees summon Jensen Huang over reported China targeting: The Information**
Leaders of three U.S. House committees have summoned Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to a closed-door briefing later this month. The Information says the session concerns his ties to Alice Huang, a tech executive reportedly identified as a Chinese spy, after The New York Times reported last month that U.S. officials had found the Nvidia chief was targeted. The Financial Times says top Republicans asked him to brief the committees after those reports. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/jensen-huang-asked-brief-congress-alleged-chinese-spy-plot)

**OLED iPad mini, M6 iMac, and new MacBook Pros go on sale: MacRumors**
The OLED iPad mini, M6 iMac, and latest MacBook Pros that Apple unveiled in late October are on sale from today, and the first pre-orders are arriving. The 8.5-inch iPad mini, 5.4mm and 255 grams, starts at $699 for 128GB Wi-Fi; it uses an A20 Pro and carries an IP67 rating, and early reviews have criticized the 60Hz display. The M6 iMac starts at $1,499, or $1,699 for the 12-core CPU and GPU version, with Apple claiming up to twice the graphics of the prior generation. The 14-inch M6 MacBook Pro starts at $1,999; touchscreen PROLED models with M5 Pro or M5 Max start at $2,899 and $3,399, and many of those configurations show a two-to-three-week ship time online. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/06/ipad-mini-oled-and-m6-imac-available-today/)

**Google launches Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash for clips up to 15 seconds: jetstream.blog**
Google announced Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash on November 5, generally available in Google AI Studio and the Gemini API, with a sequential rollout for Google AI Ultra members in Cloud, Vids, Flow, and the Gemini app. Native clip length moves from 10 seconds to 15, set in one-second steps from 3 to 15 seconds, with multi-turn edits that keep character action and camera angle. Google priced 720p output at $0.07 a second, 30 percent below Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash. Reference inputs can include motion clips of up to 3 seconds. Source: [jetstream.blog](https://jetstream.blog/en/gemini-omni-1-2-flash/)

**Nvidia steps up accelerator tracking in Southeast Asia: Bloomberg Technology**
Nvidia is stepping up monitoring of AI accelerators sold in Southeast Asia. Bloomberg describes the move as an effort to curtail semiconductor smuggling after criticism that Nvidia has not done enough to stop shipments from illegally reaching Chinese companies. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/nvidia-boosts-chip-tracking-in-southeast-asia-to-fight-smuggling)

### Company Desk
**Google announces a $17 billion Wyoming data center with carbon capture: Carbon Herald**
Carbon Herald reports that Google announced a $17 billion data center in Wyoming paired with carbon capture. The project is a new site commitment in Alphabet's infrastructure build, separate from the Malaysia expansion reported earlier this week. Source: [carbonherald.com](https://carbonherald.com/google-announces-17b-wyoming-data-center-with-carbon-capture/)

**AWS launches Kiro bots with memory for recurring developer jobs: VentureBeat**
AWS launched Kiro bots, agentic tools with persistent memory and support for recurring development jobs. The Register cast the release as Kiro adding a bot-orchestrator identity on top of the developer workflow. Source: [venturebeat.com](https://venturebeat.com/technology/aws-launches-agentic-ai-kiro-bots-with-memory-and-support-for-recurring-development-jobs)

**Apple posts its highest Q3 smartphone revenue share, Counterpoint says: 9to5Mac**
Counterpoint Research, via 9to5Mac, says Apple recorded its highest-ever share of global smartphone revenue for a third quarter. Samsung accounted for 19 percent of industry revenue, Xiaomi 6 percent, OPPO 5 percent, and vivo 4 percent. iPhone average selling price hit $1,031, up 19 percent year over year, while Apple shipments were nearly flat. Samsung still led unit share at 22 percent to Apple's 21 percent. Research director Tarun Pathak tied the price rise to higher iPhone 18 Pro launch prices, no base iPhone 18 at launch, and September increases on older models. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/05/report-apple-captured-half-of-global-smartphone-revenue-in-q3/)

**Microsoft says attackers use agentic AI tools to abuse exposed secrets: Microsoft**
Microsoft's security blog says threat actors are using agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets. The post is the company's own account of that abuse. Source: [microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/11/05/threat-actors-use-agentic-ai-tooling-to-find-and-abuse-exposed-secrets/)

### Also Today
**iPad shipments fall 27.5 percent as the tablet market hits a three-year low: 9to5Mac**
Omdia, via 9to5Mac, says Apple shipped 11.5 million iPads in the third quarter, 36 percent of a market that fell from 41.8 million units to 32.2 million, a 27.5 percent drop for Apple and the industry's lowest level in nearly three years. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/05/report-ipad-shipments-drop-27-5-as-global-tablet-market-plunges-in-q3/)

**Formula 1's CEO expects Apple to bid for rights beyond the U.S.: 9to5Mac**

**HomeView's A18 chip is paired with 8GB of RAM: MacRumors**
MacRumors confirmed that the A18 in Apple's HomeView hub has 8GB of RAM, the same pairing as in iPhone 16 models and the MacBook Neo. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/05/apple-homeview-how-much-ram/)

Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/05/apple-arcade-crossy-road-rush/)

Agility Robotics, maker of the Digit warehouse robot, began Nasdaq trading Thursday after a $2.5 billion SPAC merger, and co-founder Jonathan Hurst said Amazon warehouse tests convinced the company it needed a robot that could work beside people. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/agility-robotics-co-founder-on-its-nasdaq-debut-lessons-from-amazon-and-the-future-of-work/)

### The Counterpoint
**Google says the systems are built to block the harm the suit describes: BigGo Finance**
Against the family's account, Google spokesperson José Castañeda said the company is reviewing the claims and takes them very seriously, and that it worked with medical professionals and academic experts so young people are pointed to support and trusted resources. Google says the systems are designed to block harmful exchanges, that crisis-like queries surface hotline information in Search, and that for Workspace for Education explicit material is filtered, sensitive queries draw on trusted sources, and SafeSearch is on for educational users under 18. The filing's own open question is narrower than the default-off Google described this week: BigGo reports the company has also said schools can toggle Gemini and Search independently, without specifying whether a ban would still leave AI Mode and AI Overviews in place. Source: [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/a835f6e4-c459-4169-9da2-9461f44e7ce6)

### The Thread: Two companies, one under-16 problem
Alphabet and Meta are both in court over products a minor can reach without a separate parent signup, and the paperwork puts dates on how those products got there.

Yahoo News Singapore carries the Google complaint at 104 pages. UA.NEWS says lawyers for the family count thousands of messages and about three months of use before the girl asked the chatbot about suicide, and that Gemini showed up inside Google search rather than as an app she went looking for. BigGo's reading of the filing puts ordinary schoolwork use in autumn 2025 and the intensification in January and February 2026. Mashable says Google turned Gemini on in August for many K-12 students using Google Classroom. The same piece cites a July Common Sense Media report that rated Search's AI Overviews and AI Mode an unacceptable risk for young users, a letter from Senators Richard Blumenthal and Josh Hawley to Sundar Pichai on promotion to school-age children, California's Adam's Law as announced in September, a New York chatbot-safety law the governor unveiled last week, and AI restrictions Los Angeles and New York City public schools set for the 2026-2027 school year.

TechCrunch reports the other case: Meta, Google, and TikTok are suing California's attorney general over a law that, if it takes effect next year, would restrict social media access for children under 16. The Yahoo coverage of the Chromebook suit also says a jury ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after finding the company liable for deceiving users about privacy and content moderation on Facebook.

The shared piece is distribution, not a joint product. Google's exposure in the complaint runs through a required school laptop and through Search. Meta's exposure in the California suit runs through the social feed that statute would limit under 16. One filing treats a chatbot already on school hardware as a defective product. The other asks a court to stop a state access rule before next year. The $25 billion New Mexico result sitting in the same coverage is a jury finding about deception on Facebook, not about a chatbot. For Alphabet, the complaint's theory is that the student did not seek the bot out. For Meta, the statute would cut under-16 access on a calendar the state already set, next year, if the companies do not win the pre-enforcement case. Source: [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/05/meta-google-and-tiktok-sue-california-ag-over-teen-social-media-law/)

### On the Calendar
Leaders of three House committees want Jensen Huang in a closed-door briefing later this month on the reported China targeting. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/20119746-a285-482e-a0ae-336ce13b26bc?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Hon Hai's October sales rose 46 percent on resilient Nvidia server demand.**

**What You Need to Know:** Hon Hai's October sales rose 46 percent on resilient Nvidia server demand. Amazon turned Hive-to-Iceberg migration into a managed S3 Tables job, and Apple turned on cancellation-flow offers for App Store subscriptions. Delhi Police have an FIR over alleged child sexual abuse material on Meta's Facebook and Instagram.

### Top News
**Nvidia Partner Hon Hai’s Sales Rise 46% Thanks to AI Demand: Bloomberg Technology**
Hon Hai Precision Industry reported a 46 percent jump in October sales. Bloomberg tied that jump to resilient demand for the Nvidia servers at the center of the global AI infrastructure build-out. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-05/nvidia-partner-hon-hai-s-sales-rise-46-thanks-to-ai-demand)

**Amazon S3 Tables now offer managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg: Amazon Web Services**
Amazon S3 Tables now run a managed migration of Apache Hive tables to Apache Iceberg for Parquet tables in Amazon S3 that are registered in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. AWS says the path needs no pipelines to build and no compute to provision, and that production workloads keep running. Before any copy, S3 Tables identify every source object in scope and generate a compatibility report, then handle validation, compatibility checks, type conversions, file recompression, and compaction. Syncs can run as often as needed without stopping writes to the source, except for a few minutes at cutover. The destination stays read-only during migration and becomes read-write once migration is completed. Customers pay only for data copied, with no charge for the Hive-to-Iceberg conversion, and source objects in S3 Intelligent-Tiering stay in their current access tier. It is available in US East (Northern Virginia and Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Singapore, Sydney, and Tokyo), and Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, and Stockholm), for Glue-registered Parquet Hive tables in the same account and Region. Query paths named in the post include Amazon Athena and Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio. Microsoft made the opposite capital call. The Financial Times reported that Microsoft rejected a multibillion-dollar AI deal with the UK start-up Nscale, turning down an option to more than double a Texas data-centre contract. The paper called it a fresh blow ahead of the start-up's IPO. One of the seven is raising a new currency of debt into the build. Amazon and Meta show up again as the customers a phone-chip company wants next. The same piece said smartphone sales were tanking by around 20 percent compared with 2025. The data-center pitch is the replacement story for a phone market that shrank by about a fifth in a year.

The chip-shipment tally points the same way, and it pulls Apple in. Counterpoint Research, as reported by 9to5Mac, found Apple and Samsung were the only major smartphone-chip vendors to gain share in the third quarter of 2026, while global shipments declined 21 percent year over year. Share gained inside a falling total is not a larger phone market. It is a reshuffle while Qualcomm talks up halls instead of handsets.

What is shared is the bill for AI sites and the slump in the phone business that used to fund these suppliers. Meta is paying for the build with euro debt that buyers bid to a record and then marked above par on day one. Microsoft is choosing which contracted expansion not to take, and that choice hits Nscale before an IPO rather than adding a doubled Texas site to Microsoft's own book. Amazon and Meta are named partners for a chip vendor whose phone sales are down hard against last year. Apple's gain is mix: more of a smaller shipment pool, not a phone cycle that rescues the old line.

What changes, without treating the assembler print as the payoff, is who holds the next constraint. Meta has a euro curve it did not have. Microsoft's refusal means the extra Texas capacity in that option is not Microsoft's to switch on. Amazon and Meta become the design-in targets for a vendor exiting a weak phone year. Apple can take vendor share and still sit in a market whose units fell. None of these filings dates the quarter when the data-center spend The Verge called unrewarded starts to throw off the returns the earnings calls promised. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Google will switch off Search for students aged five to eighteen unless schools opt in.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google will switch off Search, with Gemini, for students aged five to eighteen unless a school administrator opts in. Apple put GitHub Copilot inside the Xcode 27.3 beta and testers got the iOS 27.3 build, including a China Apple Intelligence beta. A funding scrap for AI capacity runs through a Malaysian build, a first euro bond, and a thin Nvidia allocation to China.

### Top News
**Google will turn student Search and Gemini off unless schools opt in: The SOFX Report**
Starting next year, Google will leave Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search off for student accounts aged five to eighteen unless an administrator turns a service on. Chris Phillips, vice president of education, told The New York Times that Search and AI are deeply integrated, and that a school which bans AI will not have access to Search. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Google is trying to use monopoly power to force AI into public schools. Former Federal Trade Commission chair Lina Khan said Google is using its search monopoly to coerce schools into adopting AI, and that it will punish those who do not fall in line. The Decoder put the Search consequence in 2027. Google said schools should get more information on the change in the coming months. Source: [sofx.com](https://www.sofx.com/google-to-block-search-access-for-schools-that-disable-ai-features/) · [cybernews.com](https://cybernews.com/tech/google-search-ai-schools/) · [the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/schools-that-turn-off-googles-ai-will-lose-search-too-starting-in-2027/) · [sfist.com](https://sfist.com/2026/11/03/google-playing-hardball-with-schools-says-if-they-disable-ai-tools-they-cant-use-search/)

**Xcode 27.3 beta adds GitHub Copilot to Apple’s coding assistant: 9to5Mac**

Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/11/03/xcode-27-3-adds-github-copilot-to-its-built-in-coding-assistant/) · [dataconomy.com](https://dataconomy.com/2026/11/04/apple-adds-github-copilot-to-xcode-273-beta/)

**Jailbreak demo holds through Lockdown Mode and an update: MacRumors**
Hacker team Calif showed a jailbroken iPhone 18 Pro with Lockdown Mode on, then installed iOS 27.2, and the jailbreak was still in place. The video shows a malicious PDF sent by AirDrop and accepted by the user. Apple told TechCrunch earlier this year it was not aware of any successful mercenary spyware attack on an iPhone in Lockdown Mode. Calif said it is disclosing the vulnerabilities to Apple and does not plan to release a jailbreak tool for end users. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/03/iphone-jailbreak-lockdown-mode/)

**Thai opposition leaders demand a spyware answer after Apple alerts: Bloomberg Technology**
Two Thai opposition leaders want the government to disclose whether state agencies targeted political leaders with spyware, after Apple software flagged attempted attacks on their phones. The demand comes ahead of a December no-confidence debate. ### Company Desk
**Washington notice lists 95 Amazon Stores cuts, not a new round: GeekWire**
A notice made public Tuesday lists about 95 Amazon job cuts in Washington state, and a spokesperson told GeekWire they are part of previously reported Stores layoffs, not a new round. The filing names software engineers, product managers, and program managers, mostly in Seattle, with others in Bellevue, Redmond, Sumner, Pasco, or remote. Reuters had reported fewer than 1,000 corporate cuts, mainly in Stores, affecting the United States, India, and the United Kingdom. Amazon eliminated about 14,000 corporate roles globally in October 2025, including 2,303 in Washington, then a January round that included 2,198 Washington employees. Spokesperson Brad Glasser said the company adjusted parts of Stores so the structure would better match its priorities. Separately, Amazon announced roughly 300,000 seasonal openings in U.S. operations, with health coverage from January 1, 2027, for seasonal employees working at least 30 hours a week, plans starting at $5 a week with $5 copays, after a September announcement of more than $1.5 billion in additional pay for U.S. operations employees. ### The Counterpoint
**Google says schools can switch Search on without taking every AI service: The SOFX Report**
Against the reading that a school which refuses AI loses Search, Google’s news account said the day’s changes give schools more choice, not less: Gemini, Gemini Notebook, and Search start off, and administrators can turn on one, two, or all three individually. The same post said AI Mode and AI Overviews in school Search will offer step-by-step guided learning so students do not get quick answers to schoolwork. That clarification is the fact that decides whether Phillips’s “deeply integrated” line still means Search cannot be separated from Gemini. Source: [sofx.com](https://www.sofx.com/google-to-block-search-access-for-schools-that-disable-ai-features/)

### The Thread: Cheques, sites, and a chip book that will not fill
Alphabet’s Google plans to spend $15 billion to expand data-center and cloud operations in Malaysia, Bloomberg reported, with the AI boom cited as the demand pulling that infrastructure. The same country, the same day, got a different Amazon move: BusinessToday said AWS launched Semarak AI Malaysia, a program with three pillars to drive AI adoption. One figure is a construction budget. The other is an adoption program, and the launch line does not attach a dollar total to those three pillars.

Meta is raising money rather than breaking ground in that story. Bloomberg said Meta has started its first euro-denominated bond sale and is set to pay generous yields, after a $15 billion dollar deal. The wire put that debut inside a race in which the biggest technology companies are financing trillions of dollars of investment in artificial intelligence. The euro sale does not add a Malaysian hall. It adds a second currency after the dollar raise, and it prices the funding at a yield Bloomberg called generous.

Nvidia’s bind is production. Yesterday the company told cloud clients to take on less China business. Today Bloomberg reported that Chinese AI developers expect to receive 1 percent of the $70 billion in advanced RTX chips they have ordered over the next several months, because Nvidia is struggling to lift output against soaring demand. AMD, which the same wire called a key challenger to Nvidia in AI chips, forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $17 billion, plus or minus 3 percent. Bloomberg read that outlook as fresh evidence that data-center processor demand is still strong. The AMD figure is a rival’s sales line, not a count of Nvidia boxes landing in China.

On the U.S. side of the land rush, MyNorthwest identified AWS as the buyer behind a $264 million data-center land deal in West Richland, Washington. That is a site purchase. It is not a switched-on cluster, and it is not the Malaysian program.

The shared constraint is the AI capacity race: power and buildings on one side, chips and the debt that pays for both on the other. Google is committing owned cloud capacity in Malaysia. Amazon is buying land in Washington and, separately, wrapping an adoption push around Malaysia. Meta is testing whether euro investors will fund the same build after the dollar deal. Nvidia cannot turn the China slice of that RTX order book into shipments at anything like the order size, even as a challenger’s quarterly outlook says buyers who can get processors are still spending.

What changes is the queue, not a single campus opening. Malaysian capacity becomes a Google spend. Euro bond buyers become a new price on Meta’s AI funding. Chinese developers holding RTX orders are the customers for whom almost the whole book does not convert on this run. Amazon’s West Richland outlay secures dirt, not racks. No source today dates a ribbon-cutting on either site. The clock a wire actually set is the delivery window on those fractional Nvidia shipments. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/google-to-spend-15-billion-in-malaysia-data-center-expansion) · [businesstoday.com.my](https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2026/11/04/aws-launches-semarak-ai-malaysia-with-three-pillars-to-drive-ai-adoption/) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/meta-starts-debut-euro-bond-sale-after-15-billion-dollar-deal) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-04/nvidia-china-clients-to-get-1-of-70-billion-rtx-chips-ordered) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-03/amd-sales-forecast-tops-estimates-on-soaring-ai-chip-demand) · [mynorthwest.com](https://mynorthwest.com/money/aws-richland-datacenter-264m/4294306)

> **Nvidia told cloud clients a majority of their customers must be non-Chinese.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia told cloud clients a majority of their customers must be non-Chinese, a client-mix rule that would narrow one route China's AI developers use to reach advanced computing. Apple guided holiday-quarter revenue growth of 7% to 10%, above the 6% estimate in a Financial Times report, and a gross margin of 45% to 46%, below that report's 47% estimate, with John Ternus calling memory costs unprecedented. An adviser to Europe's highest court said Gemini's reuse of press articles may infringe publisher rights in some cases, while training itself stays inside the text-and-data-mining exception.

### Top News
**Nvidia tells cloud clients a majority of customers must be non-Chinese: Financial Times**
The Financial Times reported that Nvidia told cloud computing providers a majority of their clients must be non-Chinese. The Information, citing three people familiar with the matter, said Nvidia recently told some cloud customers to reduce exposure to Chinese companies, in part narrowing a key route for China's AI developers to advanced computing power. Bloomberg reported the same Financial Times account, citing unidentified people, as an instruction to scale back that exposure. Source: [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/1902df70-1380-4588-bad5-171352b575f2?syn-25a6b1a6=1) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/nvidia-tells-cloud-clients-take-less-china-business) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-03/nvidia-tells-data-center-clients-to-trim-china-business-ft-says)

**Apple guides holiday growth of 7% to 10% as memory costs cut the margin: MacRumors**
On his first earnings call as chief executive, John Ternus, with chief financial officer Kevan Parekh and chief operating officer Sabih Khan, guided December-quarter revenue growth of 7% to 10%, above the 6% estimate carried in the Financial Times report, and a gross margin of 45% to 46%, below that report's 47% estimate. The Information reported September-quarter revenue of $114.5 billion, up 12% from a year earlier, and called it the year's slowest sales growth; MacRumors put September gross margin at 47.9%. Ternus said memory pricing is "unprecedented," that memory purchase prices keep rising beyond the December quarter, and that the holiday margin also takes Siri AI costs. Inventory more than doubled year over year to $14.5 billion, and Ternus said manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33 billion from June to the September quarter. Khan said iPhone Duo is constrained and that it is hard to predict when supply and demand balance; Ternus told Reuters Apple is not able to predict that balance, and he said a very small percentage of units were returned over display issues. Greater China revenue rose 21% to a quarterly record, driven by iPhone and Mac, while Bloomberg reported Chinese revenue still fell short of estimates. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2117566404958576819) · [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/02/apple-q4-2026-earnings-takeaways/) · [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/02/apple-memory-costs-increase-december/) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/apple-sales-cool) · [techcrunch.com](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/02/apple-says-its-hard-to-predict-when-iphone-duo-constraints-will-improve/) · [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-03/apple-sets-new-sales-highs-in-china-even-as-increased-costs-bite)

**EU court adviser says Gemini's use of press may infringe publisher rights: Reuters**
Advocate General Maciej Szpunar told Europe's highest court on Tuesday that Google's Gemini may infringe press publishers' rights in certain circumstances. He said the right may be infringed when an LLM-driven chatbot retrieves a publication from a press publisher's website, reuses it to generate an answer, and gives that answer to the user. Copyright, he said, does not protect the mere facts in a news report, only the specific form of expression. Use of copyrighted material to train large language models is, in his view, freely permitted under the text and data mining exception. He was advising in a case brought by Hungarian site operator Like Company against Google, and advocate-general opinions are usually followed by the judges. Source: [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/world/googles-use-press-by-ai-chatbot-may-infringe-copyright-rules-eu-court-adviser-2026-11-03/) · [thestandard.com.hk](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/world/article/347365/Googles-use-of-press-by-AI-chatbot-may-infringe-copyright-rules-EU-court-adviser-says)

Google severed ties with Android TV box maker Videostrong and banned the company. The action followed a finding that Videostrong intentionally preloaded a malware backdoor used to control the XCPE botnet. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Techmeme/status/2117570188594008420)

### Company Desk

### Top News
**CMA opens a Meta investigation over publisher content for AI: The Next Web**
The UK Competition and Markets Authority on Friday opened a Competition Act 1998 investigation into whether Meta holds a dominant position and is imposing terms that let it collect content from the websites of businesses and publishers that use its services, then use that content in its own products, including AI, without those businesses choosing whether or how it is used. Sarah Cardell, the CMA's chief executive, said digital platforms help UK businesses reach millions of customers, but a company with a dominant position must not use it to impose unfair terms. The watchdog said the terms could be an unlawful imposition of unfair trading conditions on thousands of UK businesses, and it acted on concerns from the News Media Association and the Movement for an Open Web. Meta had planned the terms for 30 October, pushed them to 20 November after talks with the CMA, and on 28 October paused the rollout until it has consulted industry groups. In Norway, a court earlier in the week temporarily banned Meta from enforcing the new terms after 10 media outlets argued the terms threatened their rights to their content. Separately, the CMA is asking Meta for information about Meta One, its business subscription, after the Federation of Small Businesses raised concerns about small firms posting external links on Facebook and Instagram without paying; the regulator has not decided on formal action, and that question sits outside the new investigation. ### The Thread: Two backlogs, one cash test
Google Cloud's backlog climbed 256 percent to $561 billion. Amazon Web Services' backlog rose 189 percent to $578 billion. Together those stocks of contracted work are about $1.14 trillion, the figure Goldman Sachs strategists Mark Wilson and Tony Pasquariello are split on, TokenPost reported.

Google Cloud revenue increased 103 percent year over year. AWS revenue grew 39 percent. Wilson argues that the growth rates and the backlogs show AI demand remains strong and that returns are beginning to materialize at the large cloud providers. He also treats the figures as an answer to doubts about whether AI investment is paying off. Pasquariello argues the other side of the same print. Cloud growth, he says, may conceal weakness in other core businesses. Rising capital spending at technology companies has not, in his view, demonstrated comparable earnings-growth potential. He points to slower upward revisions to forward earnings-per-share estimates, and to signs that S&P 500 earnings growth may have peaked.

The cash number sitting next to the backlog is Alphabet's, not a blended cloud total. Alphabet recorded a $910 million free cash flow outflow for the quarter, compared with market expectations for a $3.5 billion inflow. Goldman Sachs strategist Rich Privorotsky framed the industry question as which companies in AI will capture the profits, and what financing costs they will face. In October, the S&P 500 excluding AI stocks outperformed technology shares. Both strategists described market volatility as unusual. They differed on whether the AI rally would continue.

The shared object is the backlog: work customers have committed to that has not yet been recognized as revenue. Both clouds are using that stock to show that AI capacity has buyers lined up, and both are still in the build. They are not the same shape of business. Alphabet's cloud revenue is the faster of the two, up 103 percent, and its backlog of $561 billion is the one that jumped 256 percent. Amazon's cloud grew 39 percent, and its backlog is the larger pile, $578 billion, up 189 percent. The $1.14 trillion sum is the joint claim. What it changes for Alphabet is already a cash result: an outflow of $910 million in a quarter when market expectations had been an inflow of $3.5 billion. What it changes for Amazon is that a $578 billion backlog now has to be read against Pasquariello's warning that cloud strength can hide slower earnings momentum elsewhere, while capital spending still runs ahead of the profit it is supposed to produce. Wilson reads the combined figure as returns starting to form. Pasquariello reads it as a mask. Privorotsky's financing-cost question hangs over both, because a backlog is a delivery promise, and delivery on this scale is being built with other people's capital as well as the cloud providers' own cash.

### The Thread: The flash shelf flipped
Two years ago Apple bought nearly twice the flash storage of Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Google combined, according to TechInsights estimates in a Wall Street Journal report carried by MacRumors. Hyperscalers are now buying double Apple’s share. That is the shared component under iPhones and under the data centers those four companies are filling.

As the iPhone took off, Apple became the world’s largest buyer of flash storage and used the leverage. The Journal account says that after ordering flash at rock-bottom prices, Apple would refuse delivery at times if prices were falling, leaving suppliers holding unsold chips, including ones custom-made for Apple. Kioxia, previously Toshiba Memory, had executives who joked they felt like Charlie Brown trying to kick the football. Apple is also said to have pressed flash makers to open their books so it could monitor sales and check that no one else got a better deal. Around the end of 2015, Sandisk refused requests for additional supply because it already had customers willing to pay more. Tony Blevins, then head of procurement, threatened a Sandisk salesman and said he would have Sandisk’s chief executive, Sanjay Mehrotra, crawl on his knees back to Apple, according to a person familiar with the call. SK Hynix and Samsung were not in those examples.

The AI data-center build is what reversed the table. Flash storage and RAM now go into those centers in volume, and the buyers on the other side of TechInsights’ old comparison — Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, and Google — are the hyperscalers whose combined purchases have passed Apple. Apple has raised prices on more than a dozen products this year, including iPhones, iPads, Macs, HomePods, and the Apple TV, and attributed the increases to the memory chip shortage. Former CEO Tim Cook said the price increases were unavoidable. An Apple spokesperson told the Journal that Apple has worked with many suppliers for decades, values the partnership, and looks forward to continuing the work.

The margin on the upgrade customers actually buy is already thinner. TechInsights estimated that Apple makes a gross profit of 134 dollars when a customer spends 200 dollars to move an iPhone 18 Pro from 256 gigabytes to 512 gigabytes, down from 185 dollars on the equivalent upgrade for the iPhone 17 Pro last year. Higher shelf prices can mean lower demand, so Apple is not fully insulated from the shortage it is passing on. On an earnings call this week, SK Hynix forecast that the memory chip shortage will persist through 2030. MacRumors read that as the bargaining pendulum staying away from Apple for at least four more years. The dated marker in the supplier’s own forecast is 2030. Strands Box, in preview, is an open-source sandbox for rules on agent behavior and access, meant to hold on a desktop, in AgentCore, or elsewhere.

**Google's Gemini 4 Carbon promises a leap in coding and cyber defence: Engadget**
Google released Gemini 4 Carbon on top of Gemini 4 Argon, which it launched two weeks earlier, and Koray Kavukcuoglu, SVP at Google DeepMind and chief AI architect at Google, called Carbon the company’s strongest model, with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon work. Access starts this week with selected cyber-defence teams, then trusted partners through the Fairwind programme, while Google says it is in the US government’s voluntary pre-release testing process; Argon is already in the Gemini app and AI search mode, and no wide Carbon date was set. Google says Carbon scored 59 on version 5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and GPT-6 Astra at 57, up from Argon’s 50. On tests Google cited, Carbon scored 88.2 percent on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8 percent on ExploitGym and 71.0 percent on CWE-bench, with secure-code success more than double Argon’s and the Chrome team reporting patch quality more than ten times that of another lab’s large frontier model. Introductory pricing matches Argon at 2 dollars per million input tokens and 10 dollars per million output tokens, cached input 95 percent below the standard input rate, and Basic Tutorials reported those rates later rise to 4 dollars and 20 dollars. NewsCord said pre-orders open October 30 and the machines launch November 6. Johny Srouji called the machine a monumental step forward for the Mac, John Ternus introduced it after taking over from Tim Cook last month, and NewsCord recalled Steve Jobs calling touchscreen Macs ergonomically terrible — “your arm wants to fall off” — and Tim Cook comparing a laptop-tablet combination to a refrigerator and a toaster. ### The Thread: Two cloud lines, one September quarter
Google Cloud revenue more than doubled in the September quarter, to over 30 billion dollars, and that unit’s operating income tripled to 11.12 billion dollars. Azure revenue in the same period was 33 billion dollars, up 48 percent. Yesterday the open question on this show was still the growth rate; those two lines are the answer, and they leave the long-time number-three cloud business a few billion dollars from Azure.

Alphabet reported a 25 percent rise in company revenue to 127.58 billion dollars, slightly short of Wall Street forecasts, The Information wrote. Free cash flow turned negative by more than 9 billion dollars, against positive free cash flow of more than 24 billion dollars a year earlier. Search advertising grew 12 percent to 63.35 billion dollars, the softest growth in that business since the second quarter of 2025. Sundar Pichai said year-over-year search-query growth is the highest in five years, and he credited AI investment. Philipp Schindler told analysts that strong growth in AI Mode queries weighed on the result because monetization there is lower: Google is not showing as many ads in AI Mode as it does in ordinary search.

The cloud comparison is not a pure hosting match. Google Cloud’s revenue includes tensor-processing-unit systems that customers install in their own data centres. It did call those sales a meaningful contributor to revenue growth. Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud’s chief executive, said the company is seeing extraordinary demand, and executives told analysts to expect TPU sales to count for even more of Google Cloud next year.

Microsoft’s September-quarter revenue rose 19 percent to 92.3 billion dollars, one percentage point faster than the growth rate reported for the prior quarter, a figure Digitimes also carried. Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud, the line that includes Copilot and the broader Office suite, rose 17 percent to 27.7 billion dollars, a slight acceleration from the June quarter. What Microsoft did not repeat was the paid Copilot seat count it had published before: 30 million at the end of June, up from 15 million at the end of 2025, each paying 30 dollars a month on top of the application fees. Satya Nadella said the number of customers paying for usage-based Copilot features grew 75 percent in the September quarter. CFO Amy Hood said average revenue per user rose because of that pay-as-you-go use. Late last month Microsoft folded Copilot features into one application, in part to steer people toward agents and usage billing, including tools set against Meta’s Muse.

Both companies are funding the same kind of build, and the quarter shows different proofs. Google’s cash flow went negative while cloud operating income tripled, and part of the cloud line is now chip hardware leaving the building. Microsoft kept commercial-cloud growth in the teens and stopped publishing the seat count that had been the simple evidence subscriptions were absorbing the spend. The next marker Kurian gave analysts is next year, when TPU sales are expected to weigh more on Google Cloud. **Google DeepMind Releases Genie 4 World Model With Real-Time Editing and Audio: AI Insider**
Google DeepMind has released Genie 4 in research preview for trusted testers. Users steer with keyboard controls and plain-language prompts, including mid-simulation changes to weather, camera, people and objects, and the model generates ambient sound, music and dialogue with the picture. MarkTechPost reports scene consistency of up to two minutes, double Genie 3, which it says ran at 720p and 24 frames per second with visual memory of about one minute after an August 2025 announcement. Gemini Omni anchors look and behavior; Gemini 3.8 Flash breaks a goal into steps, checks frames and replans if the user intervenes, and in one demo Gemini 4 Argon split a checkers task into steps that Genie 4 simulated with Apptronik's Apollo humanoid. Research director Tejas Kulkarni said future world models will be hybrids, with Gemini writing code and text while Genie simulates reality. All Genie 4 video and audio will carry SynthID watermarks; a waitlist is open, Google AI Ultra subscribers are due to get it in Project Genie, and early-access Gemini API and Google AI Studio partners follow, with The Hindu listing uses from creative direction and historical scenes to simulation after internal safety evaluations. Source: [theaiinsider.tech](https://theaiinsider.tech/2026/10/28/google-deepmind-releases-genie-4-world-model-with-real-time-editing-and-audio/)
Source: [marktechpost.com](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/28/google-deepmind-genie-4-world-model/)

**Apple Unveils M6 iMac With Faster AI Performance, Starts at $1,499: Techeconomy**
Apple has unveiled a 24-inch iMac with the M6 chip, starting at $1,499, with pre-orders from Wednesday, October 28, in 35 countries and regions and deliveries from November 6. Apple says on-device AI is up to five times the M4 iMac, graphics up to twice the M4 model, performance up to 18 times the most popular Intel-based iMac, and LM Studio prompt processing up to 12 times the M1 iMac, with memory bandwidth of 170GB per second and SSD speeds up to twice the prior generation. A 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU model starts at $1,499; a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU model, two more cores than the previous generation, starts at $1,699, with education pricing of $1,449 and $1,599. The 4.5K Retina display is rated at 500 nits in seven colors, with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, macOS 27, a 12-megapixel Centre Stage camera, up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports and support for two 6K external displays. A 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 starts at $1,999 and is due November 6, and 9to5Mac reports that iMac and that MacBook Pro keep the previous generation's prices. MacRumors says those pre-orders open at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time, and Bloomberg, via MacRumors, expects still-unannounced OLED touchscreen MacBook Pros to be announced at today's "Pro and tell" event in Los Angeles, with expected prices from $2,899 for 14-inch and at least $3,399 for 16-inch; the already unveiled OLED iPad mini, from $699, opens for pre-order on the same clock. The FIA has named Amazon Web Services its official partner for artificial intelligence, cloud computing, machine learning and cloud infrastructure, from club racing through Formula 1. AWS will help shape technical rules for the next generation of Formula 1 cars; the FIA already runs aerodynamic simulations on AWS high-performance computing so engineers can test airflow without building parts, and AWS will give technical teams AI tools for rules on safety, performance and sustainability. The agreement is separate from AWS's deal with Formula 1's commercial rights holder, cloud provider since 2018. FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said the partnership can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part. Ndoc is built on fine-tuned open-source models, keeps context across people, documents, teams and companies, and Patel plans to open-source a .ndoc.html format, which he tied to leaving rather than seeking consensus from hundreds of people at Meta. The startup has a team of three, has not raised outside funding, is in an enterprise pilot and limited alpha, and has connectors to import data from existing apps, with a beta expected in the coming weeks and a full launch in 2027. ### The Counterpoint
**A few minutes, and no ground truth: Trending Topics**
DeepMind's own limits, as MarkTechPost lists them, cut against reading Genie 4 as a place to train agents for long: interaction lasts a few minutes, not an extended session, and visual detail and object permanence drift in longer runs, after complex prompt edits, or during navigation, with real-time audio accuracy still unsolved. Trending Topics cites AI writer Ben Dickson, who argues a generated world has no ground truth to check against, so errors in the model could compound when robots are trained in it. The two-minute consistency mark is double Genie 3's visual memory, not a solved session. Source: [trendingtopics.eu](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/google-genie-4-world-model/)
Source: [marktechpost.com](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/28/google-deepmind-genie-4-world-model/)

### The Thread: A prospectus, a reseller, and next year's TPU revenue
The Information reports that Anthropic's IPO prospectus records a plan to spend $114.5 billion with Google Cloud, and the filing does not split out how much of that sum is tensor processing unit compute. The same prospectus estimates a further $125 billion to $150 billion on TPUs with Google and other providers, and $161.2 billion for TPU compute with Broadcom, which co-designs the chips with Google. TPUs began as chips Google used only internally, starting more than a decade ago. Outside customers first reached them through Google Cloud in 2018.

Oracle is the new reseller in that stack. The Information says Google has said Oracle will be the first major cloud provider besides Google itself to offer TPUs to customers from Oracle's own data centers. Google began recognizing revenue from selling TPUs into outside data centers last quarter. Chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said on that earnings call that only a small portion of revenue from those agreements showed up in the quarter, and that the vast majority kicks in next year.

John Blackledge of TD Cowen, in a report The Information cites from earlier this month, estimates TPU sales of $9.4 billion in the second half of this year, about 13 percent of the roughly $70 billion he forecasts for Google Cloud in that half. By 2028 he thinks TPUs could be a $138 billion business, 34 percent of his Google Cloud revenue estimate for that year. Analysts, on average, expect Nvidia to report $692 billion of revenue in the fiscal year ending January 2028. The Information notes that Blackledge's 2028 TPU figure would still be a fraction of that Nvidia total. Those are his estimate and the analysts' average, not figures Google or Nvidia have booked.

Meta is already a tenant on the same chip. The Information says it reported earlier this year that Meta struck a deal to rent TPUs from Google. Alphabet therefore has three commercial paths in one piece of reporting: a cloud commitment from Anthropic at prospectus scale, a sale channel through other companies' data centers with most of that revenue still ahead, and an existing rental with Meta. Nvidia's side of the comparison is the analyst revenue number, not a new chip announcement in this article. Oracle's role is to put Google silicon in a second cloud's buildings. The next dated marker the source names is next year, when Ashkenazi said the vast majority of outside-data-center TPU agreement revenue is due to be recognized. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Nvidia will invest three billion dollars in Meta to scale Muse agents.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia will invest three billion dollars in Meta’s equity offering and the two companies are expanding work on Muse, including more Vera Rubin hardware. Microsoft opened a voluntary exit to about 60,000 eligible employees in four countries. Apple unveiled the iPad mini that had circulated as an OLED rumor, now with a shipping design, chip and price.

### Top News
**Nvidia puts $3 billion into Meta and expands the Muse partnership: NVIDIA Newsroom**
Nvidia will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering, a planned commitment rather than a completed sale, as the companies expand work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve training and inference and to cut the cost of running those systems. Meta intends to expand deployment of Nvidia Vera Rubin systems and Vera CPUs for next-generation agents, plus Spectrum-X Ethernet networking and BlueField-4. The companies are also considering Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture for safer agent deployment and Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. Jensen Huang said agents are a new computing paradigm and that the partnership is meant to optimize infrastructure so Muse can serve billions of people. Mark Zuckerberg said Muse is how Meta brings personal superintelligence to everyone. Nvidia said Muse models and agents on its infrastructure have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Source: [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-and-meta-to-expand-collaboration-on-muse-and-muse-family-of-models-amid-robust-growth) · [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/briefings/nvidia-invests-3-billion-meta-deeper-ai-partnership) · [grafa.com](https://grafa.com/en/news/united-states/nvidia-meta-3-billion-investment-ai-partnership)

**Microsoft opens a voluntary exit to about 60,000 employees: Instant Gaming News**
An internal memo from chief people officer Amy Coleman launched a time-limited voluntary separation programme for eligible employees at level 70 and below on participating teams in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, about 60,000 people, roughly a quarter of the workforce. Coleman said it lets people who want a future outside Microsoft leave with support and gives participating organizations another way to match staffing to changing needs; some organizations are not offering it, and it builds on a voluntary programme earlier this year. Eligible people were to get an email with the terms. ### The Thread: Three cheques, one crowded shelf
Almost a quarter of a trillion dollars is the sum The Information put on three fundraising plans unveiled the same Monday, from Anthropic, SpaceX and Meta. SpaceX signed a $40 billion financing agreement with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management to lease graphics processors, which SpaceX called the largest GPU financing in history. Colleague Alex Eichenstein reported that the money is expected to run through a special purpose vehicle kept off SpaceX’s balance sheet, a structure that could limit any hit to its credit rating. Meta’s board committee, in a filing last week, said timing mattered so the company could secure capital before competitors saturate funding options, and it named a congested pipeline that includes Alphabet, SpaceX, Anthropic and OpenAI. Microsoft is the other of the seven in that piece, and the new number is take-up rather than eligibility: the global workforce is 223,000, an earlier voluntary offer went to 9,000 people and about a third accepted, and Microsoft is expected to see a smaller share this time, fewer than 20,000.

The shared constraint is the funding shelf, not a shared product. Meta’s directors treated Alphabet’s deals as occupying the same equity and debt options Meta wants to use before they fill up. Microsoft is offering exits while that window is still described as open. The Apollo lease is the article’s exhibit that a company with Elon Musk’s platform is choosing an off-balance-sheet GPU structure rather than a plain borrowing. Musk, in a post on X that The Information quotes, said debt markets in recent weeks have closed to firms whose revenue is only from AI data centers, and that more than 200 neoclouds face what he called guppy-level death and consolidation. The Information notes that the argument is self-serving: fewer neoclouds could leave more capital for SpaceX and other large names later. Apollo’s chief economist, Torsten Slok, wrote over the weekend that despite the investment and the hype, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech.

For Meta, the filing turns the raise into a race against other people’s calendars, including Alphabet’s, rather than a quiet registration. For Microsoft, the buyout math is the operational twin of the same squeeze: on the take-up the company is expected to see, the offer does not empty a quarter of a 223,000-person company. The risk the piece leaves on the table is Slok’s zero, and Musk’s warning that investor disfavor could spread from neoclouds to larger AI companies if customers keep seeing no payoff. **Unilever’s multi-agent creating customer value at global scale: Microsoft UK Stories**

Microsoft UK Stories reports that about 300,000 direct customers are served, and that 3.7 billion people use a Unilever product every day. Four agents read the message and extract the order; a fifth checks the work. Francis Castro, head of technology for customer operations, says orders in the pilots are eight times faster than before, refund claims are processed twice as fast, and new-customer onboarding has been reduced by 90 percent. **NVIDIA unveils architecture for secure enterprise AI agents: Engineering.com**

BlueField-4 runs NVIDIA Sentry, which quarantines an agent that leaves its software boundary in milliseconds and boosts agent capacity by up to 20 percent. ServiceNow said Arc, a personal long-running agent, is generally available, with policies carried to OpenShell and Sentry so access can be revoked across software and hardware within seconds. The stack is described as able to run on Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure, including Microsoft Windows via Microsoft Execution Containers, and to host agents from builders including Google, Meta and OpenAI. Tasks started on a smartphone can continue in the car through compatible Google services. Amy Fleming, president and CEO of Mazda Canada, said the aim is technology that stays in the background so the driver stays on the road. Mazda Canada’s retail network is 163 stores. ### The Thread: Two clouds inside one Korean bank
More than 2,000 servers and more than 100 services already run in Amazon Web Services for KB Financial Group. In 2020 the group became the first South Korean financial group to sign a corporate contract for AWS financial cloud, Seoul Economic Daily reports, and AWS has now invited AI executives from the group and from KB Kookmin Bank to its Executive Briefing Center.

Alphabet is already inside the same group. In July, KB worked with Google Cloud on KB Davis, a Gemini-based data analytics AI, and on KB Star Byeoli, a customer consultation AI. As internal AI services multiply, KB Kookmin Bank is trying to link AWS, Google Cloud and its own AI systems so the data those tools need can move between them.

The 2020 contract was a diversification, not a swap. KB wanted more than one cloud so a single provider could not become a single point of failure, and it wanted AWS technologies in financial services faster. The practical result was a parallel estate: AWS was added to the group platform Cleon, and the group now runs that estate of more than 2,000 servers and more than 100 services beside whatever it already had.

The newer layer is models, not racks. Amazon Bedrock lets a financial firm call an outside model, including Anthropic’s Claude, inside AWS security and management controls, without training the model itself. KB is tying internal systems to Bedrock at individual affiliates. The named ones are an AI investment-product information service at KB Asset Management, an AI development and operations platform for employees at KB Securities, and a customized real-estate information service at KB Kookmin Bank.

The sharpest build is the KB AI Dev Center, a dedicated AI software unit the bank opened in July this year. Developers describe the function they want in ordinary language. AI then supports design, coding and testing. AWS provided technical support for that development environment and for its monitoring framework, according to the paper’s sources. That is Amazon inside the bank’s software factory, not only inside its data center.

Google’s July work sits on the other side of the same factory. Davis is analytics. Star Byeoli is the customer conversation. Neither replaces Bedrock, and Bedrock does not replace them. The bank’s stated problem is the join: an environment in which AWS, Google Cloud and internal systems can share the data a given service needs. A deeper AWS briefing, which the paper says AWS proposed after taking an interest in how KB built its AI development framework, is a contest for the next workload between two suppliers the group already pays.

What changes for Amazon is a flagship financial account moving from a 2020 infrastructure contract into agent-style development, on an invitation AWS itself extended. What changes for Alphabet is that two named Gemini tools are already in the group, so any new AWS scope is won against an incumbent, not into an empty seat. What changes for KB is operational: more of the design-to-test loop sits with a vendor runtime, and the data path between the two clouds becomes the constraint on how far either assistant can go.

A KB Financial official said being invited to speak directly with senior AWS officials is itself meaningful, and that the group will look at further technical support and at how overseas financial firms use AI. The Seoul Economic Daily account is by Do Hye-won and was AI-translated from Korean; the paper warns that quotes from foreign sources may not match the original wording. The cooperation the official described is the scope still open: global practice, and more technical support for a framework that already spans both clouds. ### Top News
**iPhone Duo fails a dusty durability test: MacRumors**
JerryRigEverything's test got dust into the iPhone Duo hinge through several ingress points, and the dust overwhelmed the magnets that hold the phone shut. The bend test then left a permanent green line across the inner display, and the screen became unresponsive. The outer screen, with Ceramic Shield 2, scratched at level 7 on the Mohs scale. The inner screen managed level 2, though its matte nano-texture coating made marks disappear. Nelson, who said he has been testing folding phones since the first generation seven years ago and that most survive, said the iPhone Duo did not. **iPhone Duo teardowns show two batteries and a repair path: MacRumors**
REWA Technology and Phone Repair Guru posted the first teardown videos. The phone has two battery cells that come out with electrically activated adhesive: a larger cell rated 2,962 mAh (11.56 Wh) and a smaller one rated 1,921 mAh (7.5 Wh), for 4,883 mAh in total. REWA's labeled logic board shows Apple's A20 Pro chip and C2 cellular modem. Phone Repair Guru found the Touch ID button can be removed for repair, but called the process difficult, and said the USB-C port is fully modular. The Duo is eSIM-only worldwide. Mikael Wettercrantz, the offices' director of digitalisation, wrote on the staff intranet that using AI services without a formal contract can have consequences for information security, citing both the sensitivity of information entered and how AI-generated responses were handled. Consumer tools without a formal agreement send queries to external company servers, and U.S. law can compel those companies to hand data over. Copilot cleared a review in which the offices raised its security settings; ChatGPT and Claude did not get that treatment. Some employees can still reach both blocked tools through an internal platform the offices built. The Tax Agency and the National Board of Institutional Care have already banned consumer AI tools. The Enforcement Authority is preparing its own decision. A Transport Administration audit found roughly 10 AI services in use in a widespread and risky way. In February the European Parliament disabled ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot on parliamentary devices. Microsoft added Claude models to Copilot in early 2026; in the EU those Anthropic models default to off unless an administrator enables them, and the Government Offices have not confirmed whether Claude is switched on in their Copilot.
